pi-codemode-worker-threads.reason: CodemodeSandbox runs QuickJS in a node:worker_threads Worker, and its worker reads parentPort and workerData; wasm.js also imports node:fs/promises and node:module, which are unused when SLICC passes the compiled wasm. In SLICC the bios service worker must serve a node:worker_threads stub that wraps a module Web Worker (named slicc-worker-threads) and, inside it, gives parentPort and workerData from the first message; test/integration/shims/node-worker-threads.js is that stub, and the integration bundles alias node:worker_threads to it. The agent finds quickjs.wasm by walking up node_modules from its own module (locateWasm).
pi-codemode-worker-threads.removeWhen: pi-codemode accepts a browser Worker (or a worker factory) and never imports Node built-ins in the browser.

pi-ai-google-genai-lazy.reason: pi-ai imports @google/genai (and its tree: google-auth-library, gaxios, gcp-metadata, protobufjs, web-streams-polyfill, node-fetch, ...) only in its google-* APIs, which load through lazy dynamic imports. Seven offers only the Bedrock and Adobe providers, whose APIs (bedrock-converse-stream, anthropic-messages, openai-completions) never reach them, so slicc-bios removes @google/genai from /opt/agent with a pnpm override ('@google/genai': '-' in src/packages/agent/pnpm-workspace.yaml).
pi-ai-google-genai-lazy.removeWhen: seven adds a Google provider (drop the bios override first), or pi-ai stops depending on @google/genai.

pi-ai-google-vertex-lazy.reason: The second of pi-ai's two @google/genai importers (see pi-ai-google-genai-lazy): google-vertex.js must also stay behind a lazy dynamic import for the slicc-bios override ('@google/genai': '-') to be safe.
pi-ai-google-vertex-lazy.removeWhen: seven adds a Google provider (drop the bios override first), or pi-ai stops depending on @google/genai.

pi-mcp-stdio-node-only.reason: pi-mcp's index re-exports StdioTransport, whose module imports node:child_process, node:process and the CommonJS cross-spawn at the top. SLICC uses only StreamableHttpTransport and never constructs StdioTransport, so the slicc-bios service worker must let those load: node:* stubs and CommonJS wrapping for cross-spawn and its dependencies (which, isexe, path-key, shebang-command). The integration bundles alias node:child_process, node:process and cross-spawn to test/integration/shims/node-only.js.
pi-mcp-stdio-node-only.removeWhen: pi-mcp exports its Streamable HTTP transport without the stdio one (a subpath export or a lazy stdio module), or SLICC runs stdio servers through the kernel after slicc-kernel#68.

pi-mcp-sse-buffer.reason: StreamableHttpTransport parses SSE with consumeSseStream, which measures event sizes with Node's Buffer.byteLength, so every SSE response and the GET stream fail in a browser with 'Buffer is not defined'. patchSse() in src/mcp/sse.ts (applied by startMcp before any server connects) replaces StreamableHttpTransport.prototype.consumeSse with the same parser measuring bytes with TextEncoder; it throws, naming this entry, if consumeSse no longer calls consumeSseStream.
pi-mcp-sse-buffer.removeWhen: pi-mcp's SSE parser stops using Buffer.

pi-mcp-oauth-browser.reason: pi-mcp's OAuth flow makes its PKCE pair, and McpOAuthProvider its state, with Node's Buffer, and the oauth index imports OAuthCallbackServer, which imports node:http. SLICC never constructs the callback server (slicc-bios's node:* stubs let it load; the integration bundles alias node:http to test/integration/shims/node-only.js). It doesn't use McpOAuthProvider or the redirect half of authorizeMcp: src/mcp/oauth.ts has its own provider over the encrypted credential store, whose state() refuses so a background flow stops before it makes a PKCE pair, and beginSignIn() builds the authorization URL with a TextEncoder/btoa PKCE pair. authorizeMcp is still used for the code exchange and token refresh, which never touch Buffer unless a client secret is configured, and mcp.json refuses oauth.clientSecret. authProvider() in src/mcp/oauth.ts is adaptOAuthProvider with two changes: it passes oauth.authServerMetadataUrl to the background flow, and it turns any failure of that flow into McpOAuthAuthorizationRequiredError, so the server's row always offers a sign-in.
pi-mcp-oauth-browser.removeWhen: pi-mcp's OAuth code stops using Buffer and node:http in the browser; then use McpOAuthProvider with a credential-store McpOAuthStateStore and authorizeMcp for the redirect too.
